speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked	the Minister for Defence whether he can provide an update on Singapore's deployment to support the multinational coalition against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria in light of recent terrorist incidents across the world as well as the recent arrest of Singaporeans under the Internal Security Act.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I said that "so long as terrorist organisations can influence and induct others to their cause and do their bidding, no country is safe", and this is the reason why the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) has joined other partners to combat the spread of terrorism at its source – for the SAF, first, by deploying troops in Afghanistan against Al Qaeda and now in Iraq and Syria against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS).

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: By contributing to international efforts against jihadi terrorists, we are contributing to our own security.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Since then, efforts by the multinational coalition have weakened ISIS militarily in Iraq and Syria.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But despite this weakened position, ISIS supporters have been able to carry out over 20 attacks in countries across the Middle East, Europe, North America and Southeast Asia over the past months.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I think many of us are horrified by the attacks that have occurred.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We remember the one in Nice, France, on Bastille Day, which killed 84 people; a hostage siege in a cafe in Dhaka that saw 23 people dead.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They were working with Bahrun Naim, who is an Indonesian fighting for ISIS in Syria, who is also believed to have masterminded the attack in Jakarta early this year.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is, therefore, clear that ISIS, even from thousands of kilometres away in Iraq and Syria, poses a direct threat to Singapore's security here.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: From our region alone, we would do well to remember that about 1,000 Southeast Asians have joined ISIS.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For every terror plot we foil and would-be terrorist we arrest, we must assume that there will be more plots and more terror cells searching for new means to penetrate our defences and do harm to Singaporeans, as Senior Minister of State Desmond Lee pointed out.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: These developments underscore the harsh fact that the battle against jihadi terrorism will be a long-term challenge.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It has been 15 years since the fight against Al Qaeda began.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It may take just as long against ISIS, if not longer.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore, as with the rest of the world, will have to adjust, even as we are determined to carry on with our lives in facing these waves of global terror.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak has asked for an update and let me provide that.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore has been contributing to the counter-ISIS coalition since December 2014.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We have deployed a liaison officer to the United States (US) Central Command Headquarters, and an intelligence planner and an Imagery Analysis Team to the Combined Joint Task Force which is headquartered in Kuwait.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our KC-135R tanker aircraft has also supported the coalition's air-to-air refuelling operations, and our coalition partners have found our deployments useful and valuable.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: More recently, the coalition has identified an added need and asked SAF for medical support to coalition forces in Iraq.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This is not the first time that SAF has deployed a medical team for overseas operations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Members here will recall that SAF also sent medical teams to Afghanistan between 2008 and 2011.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In a similar way, our deployment in Iraq will augment existing coalition medical resources.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Through this deployment, our personnel will also gain good operational experience.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The exact size, composition and capabilities of the medical support team will be determined after our Needs Assessment and Survey Team has assessed the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The deployment is expected to take place in 2017 for around three months.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Soldiers from our Army Deployment Force will also be deployed to provide force protection for our medical team.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The threat posed by terrorism is a long-term one and the campaign against ISIS will not end quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As the fight against ISIS evolves, we will continue to assess the relevance and effectiveness of our contributions and work with our partners to determine how Singapore can best contribute.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Currently, we have been mainly involved in support services and, now, medical as well as informatics.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If one day Singapore were to be asked to contribute directly to the strike force, either through the Air Force or through ground forces, what would the Ministry's response be?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As I said, remember, in Al Qaeda, there were also plots against us.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And the source of that motivation, radicalisation, induction and actual resources provided, if not in know-how, manpower and money, finance from abroad.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, it is to our direct interest and our security interests.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: And I think that should be the predominant decision.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: As to how we can contribute, it depends on the circumstances.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We would like to contribute to make sure that we make a difference; not a token difference, but a real difference.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It was a very good hospital and they were actually tending to civilian injuries, both children and adults.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, that was actually part of, if you like, what we call the tooth, not the tail.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: That is not combat support, but we are actually making a difference.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: When bombs in Afghanistan where we were deployed were shot at, our troops and other coalition troops, many people depended on our Weapons Locating Radar to give them the three seconds to duck for cover.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, we will try to continue to make significant contributions.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For our current deployment, coalition partners have said that they valued our KC135R tankers.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We want to make a difference and it must make a difference to Singapore's security directly.
